title: ssh: connect to host port 22: Connection refused
summary: This message means the other computer answered no SSH connection on port 22. Usually the SSH server is not installed, not running, or blocked by a firewall. Check the SSH service on that computer and start it if it is off.

aliases.text: ssh connect to host port 22 connection refused
why does ssh say connection refused
ssh cannot connect to host linux

prerequisites: The user name and address of the computer you want to connect to
Administrator (sudo) rights on the computer that should run the SSH server

steps.explain: On your own computer, run ssh with -v to see where the connection stops. The debug lines above the error show the address and port that were used.

placeholders.name: USER
placeholders.description: User name on the remote computer

placeholders.name: HOST
placeholders.description: Address or name of the remote computer

steps.expect: Debug lines show 'Connecting to ... port 22' and then 'connect to address ... port 22: Connection refused'. Nothing answers on port 22 there.

steps.explain: On the remote computer, list the TCP ports that programs are listening on. SSH listens on port 22 when its server is running.
steps.expect: A LISTEN line ending in ':22' means the SSH server runs. No such line means nothing listens on port 22.

steps.explain: On the remote computer, check the SSH service. On Debian, Ubuntu and Mint it is named ssh; on Fedora, Arch and openSUSE it is named sshd.
steps.expect: 'Active: active (running)' means the server runs. 'could not be found' means it is not installed. 'inactive (dead)' means it is stopped.

steps.explain: Install the SSH server only if the previous step said it is not installed. This changes system software, so do it only on a computer you administer.
steps.expect: The install finishes without errors. Then repeat the service status check.

steps.explain: Start the SSH service now. Starting it lets other computers reach this one on port 22, so do it only on a computer you control.
steps.expect: No output means the service started. Confirm with the verify command below.

alternatives.explain: Start the SSH service now and also at every boot.

verify.expect: A LISTEN line ends with ':22', for example 0.0.0.0:22 or [::]:22.
The 'Connection refused' line is gone. ssh now reaches the login step, for example a password prompt or 'Host key verification failed' for a new host.

rollback.explain: Remove the SSH server package if you installed it only for this check.

warnings: An SSH server reachable from the network lets others try to log in. Use strong passwords or keys, and keep the system updated.
Even when the SSH server runs, a firewall can still block port 22. Check the firewall on the remote computer.
Connecting to the wrong address can give a different error, such as 'Connection timed out' or 'No route to host'.
